note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A client walks into the salon while you are working with another client. What should you do?
options: Carry on working and wait for the client to speak to you first
Call across the salon to ask the client what she wants done
Smile, greet her politely and tell her someone will be with her soon
Leave your client at the chair and take the new client to the basin

questions.stem: Why should you check the appointment book when a client arrives?
options: To find out how much the client paid at her last visit
To see which stylist is free to take an early lunch
To confirm her name, the service booked and the stylist
To count how many clients came in during the week

questions.stem: Where should a client's bag and shopping be kept during the service?
options: On the floor right beside the styling chair, where she can see them
On the counter at the station, next to the tools and products
Behind the reception desk, with no record of who owns them
In a safe place such as a locker or coat stand, as the salon allows

questions.stem: Which of these is an open question to use in a consultation?
options: Do you want your hair the same as last time?
How do you usually style your hair at home?
Have you used a relaxer in the last month?
Is your hair longer than shoulder length?

questions.stem: Why should you listen carefully and repeat back what the client has asked for?
options: To make sure you both agree on the result before you start
To make the consultation last longer so the dryer can warm up
To show the client that you know more about hair than she does
To give the client time to change her mind and leave the salon

questions.stem: Which body language shows the client that you are listening?
options: Looking at your phone while the client is speaking
Folding your arms and looking around the salon
Facing the client, nodding and keeping eye contact
Brushing her hair while she explains what she wants

questions.stem: A client brings a photo of a style worn by a singer. What should you do?
options: Promise that her hair will look exactly like the photo
Look at it with her and explain what will suit her hair
Tell her that photos are not allowed in the salon
Copy the style without checking her hair type first

questions.stem: Why must you ask a client about chemical services she has had, such as a relaxer, colour or perm?
options: So that you can charge her exactly what the last salon charged her
Because some products react badly with chemicals already on the hair
So that you can tell her which other salon in town is the best one to use
Because chemical services make the hair grow more slowly

questions.stem: Why do you ask a client about her job and daily routine during the consultation?
options: To decide how much she can afford to pay for the service
To have something to talk about while the hair is drying
To suggest a style she can manage and that suits her day
To write her employer's name on the client record card

questions.stem: What is hair 'porosity'?
options: How far a strand of hair can stretch and then return
How well the hair can take in and hold moisture
How many hairs grow on each part of the scalp
How thick each single hair is from side to side

questions.stem: Hair that feels rough, tangles easily and soaks up water fast is most likely to be:
options: Healthy hair with low porosity
Virgin hair with a closed cuticle
Fine hair with very low density
Damaged hair with high porosity

questions.stem: Which is the correct order of curl patterns, from the least curly to the most curly?
options: Coily, curly, wavy, straight
Straight, wavy, curly, coily
Wavy, straight, coily, curly
Curly, wavy, coily, straight

questions.stem: How do you check the condition of the client's scalp?
options: Part the hair in sections and look closely at the skin
Rub the scalp hard with your nails to feel for bumps
Ask the client to describe her scalp and skip looking
Shampoo first and then look at the scalp when it is wet

questions.stem: A client had a relaxer some months ago and now has about 5 cm of natural regrowth at the roots. Why is this important to note?
options: The two hair textures must be shampooed with two different products
Natural regrowth means the relaxer was the wrong kind to use
The regrowth shows the client is not washing her hair enough
The relaxed ends and natural roots need different care when styled

questions.stem: What is 'virgin hair'?
options: Hair that has never had a chemical service such as colour or a relaxer
Hair on a young child that has never been cut by a stylist before
Hair that has just been shampooed and has no styling product left on it
Hair that has grown back after a short haircut last month

questions.stem: Why is a skin (patch) test done before a hair colour service?
options: To check how quickly the colour will develop on the hair
To see what shade the colour will turn out on the client
To find out how long the colour will last on the hair
To check whether the client is allergic to the product

questions.stem: When the maker asks for a skin test before a colour service, when is it usually done?
options: At least 48 hours before
About 10 minutes before
Straight after the service
Only once in a lifetime

questions.stem: What does a strand test show before a chemical service?
options: Whether the client's skin will react badly to the product
How the hair will take the product and how long to leave it
How many sections the hair will need to be divided into
Whether the scalp has any cuts, sores or bumps on it

questions.stem: A client's skin test shows redness, swelling and itching around the test area. What should you do?
options: Go ahead with the colour, but leave it on the hair for a shorter time
Use a different shade of the same product instead
Do not do the service, record it and advise her to see a doctor
Wash the test area well and then carry out the service as booked

questions.stem: What is an incompatibility test used for?
options: To check whether the client can afford the chemical service
To check whether two stylists agree on the colour to use
To check whether the hair is long enough for the style chosen
To check for chemicals already on the hair that may react badly

questions.stem: A strand of wet hair stretches a long way and then breaks, or does not spring back. What does this show?
options: The hair is very strong and in excellent condition
The hair has a closed cuticle and low porosity
The hair is weak and may not take a chemical service
The hair has a very high density and needs thinning out

questions.stem: Which of these scalp conditions stops a salon service, with the client advised to see a doctor?
options: Ringworm, a fungal infection
Mild dandruff with small flakes
A slightly oily scalp
Grey hairs at the temples

questions.stem: What is a 'contraindication'?
options: A product that the salon recommends for home use
A list of prices for the services the salon offers
A condition that means a service should not be done
A test that shows how much the hair can stretch

questions.stem: You find head lice in a client's hair during the consultation. What should you do?
options: Stop, tactfully tell her in private, and suggest she get treatment
Carry on with the service, but use a fine comb on the hair
Announce it loudly so other clients can move away from her
Put extra conditioner on the hair to kill the lice before styling

questions.stem: A client says she is using a cream from her doctor for a skin problem on her scalp. What should you do?
options: Carry on as normal, because the doctor's cream will protect her scalp
Check with your supervisor and ask if her doctor has cleared it
Wash the cream off and put a salon product on instead
Tell her that the cream will not work on her hair type

questions.stem: Why should you check the scalp for cuts or scratches before a chemical service?
options: Because cuts make the chemical take longer to work
Because cuts change the colour the hair will turn out
Because cuts mean that the hair has been cut too short
Because chemicals can burn and get into broken skin

questions.stem: A client arrives with a high temperature and says she feels unwell. What is the right action?
options: Give her a cold drink and carry on with the service
Do the service quickly so that she can go home sooner
Advise her to rebook for when she is well again
Turn the fan on her and keep her in the waiting area

questions.stem: Why do you place a towel around the client's shoulders under the gown for a shampoo?
options: To keep the client warm in the air-conditioned salon
To soak up water so the client's clothes stay dry
To make the gown fit more tightly around the neck
To show the client which basin she should sit at

questions.stem: Which item protects a client's clothes during a chemical service such as a relaxer?
options: A waterproof chemical cape
A cotton cutting collar
A paper face mask
A thin nylon hairnet and clips

questions.stem: Why is a neck strip (or towel) placed between the client's neck and the cape?
options: To make the cape easier and quicker for the stylist to fasten
To stop the cape from slipping off the shoulders during the service
To show the client that the cape has been washed and is clean
To keep the cape off the skin and stop hair or products getting in

questions.stem: Why should the client take off earrings, necklaces and hair clips before a service?
options: So that the stylist can keep them safe in the till drawer
So that the client looks the same as in her photo
So that they are not lost, damaged or caught in the tools
So that the salon can check whether they are real gold

questions.stem: How should the client be seated for a shampoo at a back-wash basin?
options: Leaning forward, with her face over the basin
Standing at the basin with her head bent back
Sitting sideways on the chair, with her head turned to one side
Sitting back, with her neck resting on a padded basin edge

questions.stem: Why should you adjust the styling chair to the right height before you start?
options: So that you can work with a straight back and good control
So that the client can see the street through the window
So that the chair is ready for the cleaner to wipe it down
So that the client's feet can rest on the basin edge

questions.stem: What should the workstation be like before you seat a client?
options: Covered with the last client's tools so that you can reuse them
Set with any products found in the store, in no special order
Laid out with the newest tools, even if they have not yet been cleaned
Clean, with disinfected tools and the products needed for the service

questions.stem: Which items must be fresh and clean for every client?
options: The styling chair and the mirror only
The products on the shelf in the waiting area
Towels, gowns and neck strips
The appointment book and the pens

questions.stem: What is the difference between cleaning and disinfecting a comb?
options: Cleaning kills all germs, while disinfecting only removes hair
Cleaning removes dirt and hair, and disinfecting then kills most germs
Cleaning is done with a chemical, and disinfecting is done with water
Cleaning is done once a week, and disinfecting is done once a year

questions.stem: Why should a stylist wash her hands before touching each new client?
options: To stop germs from passing from one client to the next
To make her hands softer for the scalp massage
To warm her hands so the client feels comfortable
To remove the smell of the last client's products from her hands

questions.stem: What should be written on a client record card after the consultation?
options: Contact details, tests done, products used and any reactions
The client's monthly salary and the name of her employer
The stylist's own private opinions about the client's personality
Only the price she paid and the time that she left

questions.stem: A client tells you about a health problem during the consultation. What should you do with this information?
options: Share it with the other stylists so they know about her
Post about it on the salon's social media page
Mention it to the next client to make conversation
Record what is needed and keep it private

questions.stem: Why do some salons ask the client to sign the record card before a chemical service?
options: To prove the client has paid in full for the service
To give the stylist permission to use the client's photo
To show the client agreed to the service after the tests
To let the client take the salon's products home free

questions.stem: A 14-year-old wants a chemical service. Following the salon's policy, what does the salon usually need first?
options: Consent from her parent or guardian
A letter from her school about her grades
Payment in cash before the consultation
A photo of a friend with the same style

questions.stem: After the consultation, what should the client be told before the service starts?
options: The names of the other clients booked in for the day
What will be done, how long it will take and the cost
How much the stylist earns for each service she does
Which products the stylist uses on her own hair

questions.stem: A client uses a wheelchair. How should you prepare her for the service?
options: Ask her to stand up at the basin for a short while during the shampoo
Lift her into the styling chair without asking her first
Tell her the salon cannot serve clients who use wheelchairs
Ask how she prefers to be helped and adapt the setup to suit her

questions.stem: How can you make a client comfortable while she waits for her stylist?
options: Leave her alone and say nothing until the stylist is free
Offer a seat and a drink of water and tell her the wait time
Ask her to help sweep the floor so the wait goes faster
Tell her to come back later without saying how long it will be

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of preparing the client properly before a salon service?
options: To make the service take longer so that the salon can charge more for it
To give the trainee practice in talking to strangers
To keep the client safe and comfortable and get the result she wants
To make sure the stylist has time to take a break first

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name for the point on the hair shaft where natural regrowth meets hair that was relaxed before?
What is the everyday name for small, dry white flakes of skin shed from the scalp?
Which bacterial skin infection causes weeping yellow crusts and spreads easily from person to person?
Which hair test stretches a wet strand to see how well it springs back?
What kind of question can be answered with only 'yes' or 'no'?
What are the eggs of head lice called, which stick firmly to the hair shaft?
What word means keeping a client's personal information private?
What is the name of the area at the front of the salon where clients are greeted and booked in?
What is the middle layer of the hair, inside the cuticle, that gives hair its strength, stretch and colour?
What protective items should the stylist wear on her hands when applying a chemical product?
Which skin condition, which is not catching, causes red patches covered with thick, silvery scales?
What is an infection of the hair follicles called, which shows as small red or white bumps around the hairs?
What is the name of the sheet from the maker that gives a product's hazards, safe handling and first aid?
A client's appointment starts at 2:15 p.m. and the service takes 1 hour 45 minutes. At what time will it end?
What is the medical name for an allergic rash caused by a product touching the skin?

essays.stem: Describe how you would greet and receive a client who arrives for her appointment, up to the moment she is seated for the service.
essays.modelAnswer: When the client comes in, I stop what I am doing for a moment, smile and greet her politely by name if I know it. I check the appointment book or app to confirm her name, the service, the time and the stylist. I tell her if there will be a short wait and how long, and offer her a seat and a drink of water. I take her bag or coat to a safe place, such as a locker or coat stand, and remind her to keep valuables with her. I tell the stylist that the client has arrived. When the stylist is ready, I take the client to the station, help her into the chair and make sure she is comfortable. I keep a friendly, professional manner throughout and never talk about other clients in front of her.
markingPoints: Greets the client politely and promptly, with a smile
Checks the booking: name, service, time and stylist
Tells her about any wait and offers a seat and a drink
Looks after her belongings safely and tells the stylist she has arrived
Takes her to the station, seats her comfortably and stays professional

essays.stem: Explain how to carry out a consultation. Give examples of the questions you would ask and say why each one matters.
essays.modelAnswer: I sit or stand where the client can see me, face her and listen carefully. I use open questions to learn what she wants, such as 'What would you like done today?' and 'How do you style your hair at home?' This tells me the result she wants and how much time she spends on her hair. I ask 'What chemical services or colours have you had, and when?', because some products react with chemicals already on the hair. I ask about allergies, skin problems and medicines, to find any contraindications. I ask about her work and lifestyle so I can suggest a style she can manage. I use closed questions to check facts, such as 'Did you have a skin test for this colour?' I look at any photos she brings. At the end I repeat back what we agreed, with the time and the price, and write it on her record card.
markingPoints: Faces the client, listens and uses open questions to find out what she wants
Asks about past chemical services and gives the reason
Asks about allergies, skin problems and medicines to find contraindications
Asks about lifestyle, and uses closed questions to check facts
Repeats back the agreed service, time and price and records it

essays.stem: Describe a full hair and scalp analysis: what you look at, the tests you do, and what the results tell you.
essays.modelAnswer: I start by looking at the hair dry, in good light. I note the curl pattern (straight, wavy, curly or coily), the texture (fine, medium or coarse), the density, the length, and whether the hair is virgin, relaxed, coloured or a mix, for example natural regrowth on relaxed ends. I look for split ends and breakage. For porosity, I slide my fingers from the ends to the roots: rough hair is porous and will soak up products quickly. For elasticity, I gently stretch a damp strand: healthy hair stretches and springs back, while weak hair breaks or stays stretched. I part the hair in sections and look at the scalp for cuts, sores, redness, flaking, lice or signs of infection. The results tell me whether the service can go ahead, which products and heat to use, and how gentle I must be. I write the results on the record card.
markingPoints: Looks at curl pattern, texture, density and length
Notes previous chemical work and the condition of the hair
Porosity test done and explained correctly
Elasticity test done and explained correctly
Checks the scalp in sections and uses the results to plan the service, and records them

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would carry out a skin test for a hair colour, following the maker's instructions.
essays.modelAnswer: First I read the maker's instructions, because they say how and when to do the test, usually at least 48 hours before the service. I explain to the client why the test is needed. I choose the place the maker gives, such as behind the ear or the inside of the elbow, and clean a small area of skin. Wearing gloves, I prepare a small amount of the product as the maker says, and apply it to the area with a cotton bud. I let it dry and ask the client not to wash or cover it. I tell her to remove it and call the salon at once if she feels burning, itching or swelling. I write the date, time, product and place on her record card. When she comes back, I check the area. If there is any redness, swelling, itching or blistering, the test is positive and I must not do the colour.
markingPoints: Follows the maker's instructions on timing (usually at least 48 hours before)
Cleans a small area in the place the maker gives, such as behind the ear
Applies a small amount with gloves and a cotton bud, and leaves it uncovered
Tells the client what to do if it burns or itches, and records the test
Checks the result: any reaction is positive and the service must not go ahead

essays.stem: Name four conditions you might find during a consultation that mean a service should not go ahead, or must be changed. Say what you would do for each, and how you would tell the client.
essays.modelAnswer: Head lice are catching. I would not go ahead, and would advise treatment before rebooking, then clean and disinfect my tools and the area. Ringworm is a fungal infection that spreads. I would not go ahead and would advise the client to see a doctor. Impetigo is a bacterial infection with yellow crusts. Again I would not go ahead and would refer her to a doctor. Cuts or open sores on the scalp mean I must not use any chemical service, as it could burn the skin, and I might delay heat styling until the skin has healed. A positive skin test means I must not use that product. In every case I speak to the client privately and kindly, without frightening or embarrassing her. I do not try to diagnose; I say what I can see and suggest she sees a doctor. I record what I found and tell my supervisor.
markingPoints: Names four suitable conditions (such as lice, ringworm, impetigo, cuts, a positive skin test)
Gives the correct action for each, including referral to a doctor where needed
Cleans and disinfects tools and the area after an infection is found
Tells the client privately and kindly, without diagnosing
Records the finding and tells the supervisor

essays.stem: Describe how to gown and protect a client for (a) a shampoo and blow-dry and (b) a chemical service such as a relaxer.
essays.modelAnswer: For both services I first ask the client to remove earrings, necklaces and hair clips and keep them safe. I wash my hands. For a shampoo and blow-dry, I put on a clean gown and fasten it. I place a clean towel around her shoulders, then a waterproof cape over the towel, fastened firmly but not tightly at the neck. After the shampoo, I change to a dry towel or cutting collar for the blow-dry. For a chemical service, I put on a clean gown, a neck strip and a towel, then a chemical-resistant cape. I may add a second towel over the cape. Following the maker's instructions, I apply a protective base cream along the hairline and over the ears. I wear gloves and an apron myself. In both cases I check that the client is comfortable and that no clothing can get wet or stained.
markingPoints: Removes jewellery and hair clips, and washes hands
Shampoo and blow-dry: gown, towel and waterproof cape, fastened safely
Chemical service: gown, neck strip, towel and chemical-resistant cape
Protects the hairline and ears as the maker says, and wears gloves and apron
Checks the client is comfortable and her clothing is protected

essays.stem: Explain how you would prepare the workstation and tools before a client sits down, so that the service is safe and hygienic.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the booking so I know which service and products are needed. I wipe the chair, counter, armrests and mirror with a disinfectant, following the maker's instructions. I sweep up any hair and make sure the floor is dry. I set out clean, disinfected combs, brushes and clips, and fresh towels, a gown and a cape. Single-use items, such as neck strips and gloves, are new for each client. I put out only the products the service needs, with lids closed and labels facing out. I check that electrical tools work and that plugs and cables are not damaged, and I keep cables away from where people walk. I adjust the chair height and check the basin and water. Finally I wash my hands. A clean, ready station stops germs spreading, prevents accidents and lets the service run on time.
markingPoints: Checks the booking to know the service and products
Cleans and disinfects the chair, counter and mirror; floor swept and dry
Sets out disinfected tools, fresh towels and new single-use items
Checks electrical tools and keeps cables safe
Explains that this stops germs spreading, prevents accidents and saves time

essays.stem: Explain why client records are kept, what should be written on them, and how they must be stored.
essays.modelAnswer: Client records help the salon give a safe, consistent service. Any stylist can see what was done before and what worked, which saves time. They show when skin tests were done and the results, so a product that caused a reaction is not used again. They also protect the client and the salon if there is a problem later. A record should show the client's name and contact details, any relevant medical notes or allergies, the results of the hair and scalp analysis and tests, the services done with the date, products, timings and stylist, and any reactions or advice given. For chemical services, the client may sign to agree. Records must be kept private. Paper cards are stored in a locked drawer or cabinet, and computer records are protected with a password. They are only used for the client's service and are not shared or talked about.
markingPoints: Records give a safe, consistent service and show what was done before
Records show tests and reactions, and protect the client and the salon
Lists what to record: details, medical notes, tests, services, products, dates
Mentions the client's signature for chemical services
Stores records privately: locked away or password-protected, not shared

essays.stem: Describe how you would adapt your preparation for three different clients: a young child, an older client, and a client who uses a wheelchair.
essays.modelAnswer: For a young child, I make sure a parent or guardian is with them and agrees to the service. I use a booster seat so that I can work at a safe height, and use a smaller gown. I explain things simply and keep tools and products out of reach. I work gently and quickly, as children cannot sit still for long. For an older client, I give her time and speak clearly. I ask about any health problems, such as stiffness in the neck, which may make a back-wash basin uncomfortable. I offer extra support or a front-wash basin, and help her in and out of the chair. For a client who uses a wheelchair, I ask how she likes to be helped and never lift her without asking. I clear a wide path, and if she prefers to stay in her wheelchair, I adjust my position or use a portable basin.
markingPoints: Child: parent or guardian present and agrees; booster seat and small gown
Child: simple explanations, tools out of reach, gentle and quick
Older client: time, clear speech, asks about health, extra support at the basin
Wheelchair user: asks how she prefers to be helped and never lifts without asking
Wheelchair user: clear path and adapts the setup, such as a portable basin

essays.stem: Explain how you would prepare a client with natural, tightly coiled hair for a wash and style, and how this is different from preparing a client with straight hair.
essays.modelAnswer: For both clients I do a consultation, check the scalp and gown them properly. With tightly coiled natural hair, I ask how she cares for her hair at home, whether she has had any protective styles taken out recently, and what she wants: a defined curl, a stretched look or a silk press. Coily hair tangles and shrinks easily, so before the shampoo I gently finger-detangle in sections, sometimes with a little oil or conditioner, and twist or clip each section to keep it apart. I check for build-up and for breakage at the hairline. I choose moisturising products and allow more time. With straight hair, I can usually brush through before the shampoo, it tangles less, and it may get oily sooner, so I check for oil at the scalp. The tools differ too: wide-tooth combs and detangling brushes for coily hair, and a paddle brush for straight hair.
markingPoints: Consultation, scalp check and gowning for both clients
Asks the natural-hair client about home care, recent protective styles and the result she wants
Detangles coily hair gently in sections before the shampoo and keeps sections apart
Chooses moisturising products and allows more time for coily hair
Explains the differences for straight hair, including tools and products

practical1.title: Client reception, consultation and hair and scalp analysis
practical1.brief: Work as a group of 4 or 5 in the Centre's salon. Take turns in four roles: receptionist, stylist, client and observer, so that every member is the stylist once. The receptionist greets the client, checks the booking sheet and seats her. The stylist carries out a full consultation, then a hair and scalp analysis on the client (a group partner or a model who agrees), including a porosity test and an elasticity test. The stylist fills in a client record card and explains the agreed service, time and price. The observer takes the photos and notes on a sheet one thing the stylist did well and one thing to improve. Photograph only the hair, scalp, hands and paperwork, never faces, unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group with the photos, the record cards and the observer sheets.
materials: A booking sheet with each member's client listed
Blank client record cards and observer sheets
Wide-tooth combs, tail combs and sectioning clips
A spray bottle of clean water for the elasticity test
A good light, such as a lamp or magnifying lamp
photos: The reception desk with the booking sheet checked
The client gowned and seated at the station
The scalp check, with the hair parted in sections
The elasticity test being done on a damp strand
checklist: Greeted the client politely and checked the booking (as receptionist)
Used open and closed questions, including chemical history, allergies and lifestyle
Checked the scalp in sections, in good light, for contraindications
Carried out and explained the porosity and elasticity tests correctly
Recorded the curl pattern, texture, density and condition
Filled in the record card fully and clearly
Explained the agreed service, time and price to the client
Kept the client's information private and worked hygienically
safety: Wash your hands before and after touching each client's hair
Stop and tell the assessor if you find lice, sores or signs of infection, and do not go on
Do not pull hard on the hair during the elasticity test
Keep record cards private and hand them to the assessor at the end

practical2.title: Prepare the station and gown clients for a shampoo and for a chemical service
practical2.brief: Work as a group of 4 or 5 in the Centre's salon. Each member prepares one station and gowns a group partner (or a model who agrees) twice: first for a shampoo and blow-dry, then for a chemical service such as a relaxer. No chemical is applied. For the chemical service gowning, each member also shows how they would protect the hairline and ears, using a plain barrier cream the Centre provides, and shows the steps of a skin test using a plain lotion with no colour or chemical in it, then fills in a skin test record. Members take turns as the client, the photographer and the checker, who uses the group's checklist to check each step. Photograph only the work area, hands and hair, never faces, unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group when every member has finished and the stations are clean.
materials: Clean gowns, towels and waterproof capes
A plain barrier cream approved by the Centre
A plain lotion with no colour or chemical in it, and cotton buds, for the skin test practice
Disinfectant for surfaces and a laundry bin
photos: Each station cleaned and set out with disinfected tools
The client gowned for a shampoo: gown, towel and cape
The client gowned for a chemical service: gown, neck strip, towel and chemical cape
Barrier cream on the hairline and ears
The skin test steps with the plain lotion, behind the ear or on the inner elbow
The stations cleaned and used towels in the laundry bin
checklist: Cleaned and disinfected the station and set out only what the service needs
Asked the client to remove jewellery and hair clips, and washed hands
Gowned correctly for a shampoo, with the cape firm but not tight
Gowned correctly for a chemical service, with a neck strip and chemical cape
Wore gloves and an apron, and applied barrier cream neatly to the hairline and ears
Showed the skin test steps in the right order and filled in the record
Checked the client was comfortable throughout
Left the station clean, with used items in the laundry or bin
